bubbles.title: Interview pain points
bubbles.hint: Interview the human one question at a time. Pain points so far: (1) bare ??? fog leaves the human unsure what to say, uu doesn't help much; a grill-me or research step would; (2) pre-bubble track planning to avoid premature tracks, short and not a plan-mode wall of text; (3) no guards on what to change or not to touch (target files/domains), so the agent drifts; (4) vague bubbles like 'implement new parsing method' let the agent go rogue; need better seams (not one bubble per file) that also make review easier. (3a) Guards = a ruleset of what NOT to do, to focus on the real end result; hard to write while the human is still at an unknown stage. (4a) Seams: not a one-shot across many files, and size varies (one file vs several). Split per use case, within that use case's identified boundaries. (2a) The plan's output is a better track, focused on the core end-goal problem; its guards and extra context make a stable track with fewer unknowns.

bubbles.title: E2E dev track
bubbles.hint: An e2e test (test/*.test.js, temp repo) that builds a development track by running every CLI command in turn (switch/create, add, insert, fog, type, fill, hint, handoff, rename, move, remove, fork, diverge, done, close...) and asserts each step's output. Its rendered transcript doubles as material for the flow analysis.

bubbles.title: Audit skill flow
bubbles.hint: Read SKILL.md + fallback.md + CLI; map the actual steps (sketch, classify, walk, fog stop) against the interview's pain points. For each change (plan step, guards, seams, research, grill-me), decide: reusable ability or core library/CLI feature? The human is undecided.

bubbles.title: Plan step gap
bubbles.hint: Plan up front, before the first bubble: its output is a better track focused on the core end goal. Guards (what not to do) and use-case seams fall out of the plan and are stored as hints or similar, not as separate bubbles. Also a mini-plan ability for planning later in the track when needed. Audit: core. Short plan step before sketch produces goal + guards + use cases; goal and guards stored on the track (new Track fields, model.ts) and printed by show/switch; guards are soft rules the agent checks before done. Seams: skill text only, one bubble per use case, hint names its boundary; work past it → stop and propose insert. mini-plan (type: track) = ability.

bubbles.title: Subtle goal icons
bubbles.hint: Goal/guards icons: → goal, ¦ guards (ascii > and !), in the symbol sets so --ascii works. Was ◎ and ⛔.

bubbles.title: Guards on demand
bubbles.hint: Guards print only on switch (resume), after a guard command, and via guard show; not on every show/mutation. Goal line stays.

bubbles.title: E2E + agent docs
bubbles.hint: e2e steps for goal, guard, guard show; AGENTS.md rule: CLI changes extend test/e2e.test.js; CLAUDE.md that imports AGENTS.md.

bubbles.title: Research step
bubbles.hint: Should research be a built-in step (or an ability) instead of only via known-unknown fog? Audit: ability. research + grill abilities (type: bubble), offered when the human answers ? while classifying fog; uu interview already is grill-me.

bubbles.title: Fog needs a reason
bubbles.hint: Fog is sometimes created without saying why, which irritates the user. Require a one-line reason per fog bubble (hint or CLI field). Audit: core. Every fog carries a one-line reason (why it's unclear, not what it is), so 'never plan fog' holds. Fix SKILL.md step 1 'add --fog with no detail' and use add ? consistently.

bubbles.title: Update skill + docs
bubbles.hint: Apply the agreed changes to SKILL.md, fallback.md, README, and tests. Flow text lives in 5 places: SKILL.md, fallback.md, adapters/agents-md.md, adapters/gemini/bubble.toml, and CLI-printed guidance (tracks.ts fork/diverge line, print.ts fog line, bubbles.ts stop line). From bubble 4: goal/guard commands exist (CLI, help, fallback.md done). Still to write: plan step before sketch (goal + guards + use cases) in SKILL.md and adapters; guards come BEFORE acting (human, goal-guard-test): read them (guard show) before implementing a bubble or taking any action, not as a check at done; seams (one bubble per use case, hint names its boundary); mini-plan ability (type: track). Plan-step flow (agreed): switch on an existing name resumes at once (step 0 unchanged); a new name or 'I want X' gets the plan first, in chat, no track yet: 3 short questions (goal, guards, use cases) → one compact proposal (name + title, goal, guards, bubbles with fog reasons, or 'fits track X, add there?') → human ok/edits → create, goal, guard xN, add xN, hints in one burst → classify fog → ⏸. No CLI change; check tracks for the name.

bubbles.title: Goal test findings
bubbles.hint: From goal-guard-test bubble 1: (a) goal - with no goal says 'cleared the goal'; say 'no goal to clear' like guard - does. (b) changing a goal doesn't show the old one; title prints old → new. (c) the → goal icon reads like the → active-bubble marker right below it.

bubbles.title: Guard test findings
bubbles.hint: From goal-guard-test bubble 2: (a) guard 3 (likely a typo for guard 3 -) silently adds a guard titled '3'; refuse a bare number. (b) guard show extra / guard 1 - x also become guard text silently. (c) no way to edit a guard: drop + add moves it to the end. (d) guard - drops all without asking; fine for now? From bubble 3: (e) guards are pre-action rules, not a done check (human). Relabel 'guards (check before done)' to e.g. 'guards (before you act)' in print.ts, model.ts comment, help text, fallback.md, tests.

bubbles.title: Plan step findings
bubbles.hint: From goal-guard-test bubble 4. Worked: a one-line goal gave 4 use-case bubbles, no fog, no over-planning; 'Boundary:' in hints kept each bubble scoped; guard 2 routed 4 source requests (icons, guards on demand, e2e/docs, relabel) to flow-analysis, so the test track stayed clean. Fix in SKILL.md: (a) the plan asked 3 questions at once and the human answered only the goal, so the agent drafted guards and use cases; say that the agent may propose guards and use cases and the human confirms. (b) Say what guards are for: read before acting, not a done check (the human corrected this mid-track). (c) A fresh agent can't run the plan step yet; it only exists in bubble hints. Decided (human): a guard stands even against a direct human ask; route the work to the right track.
